title: Mara and the Horizon
premise: Bush pilot Marguerite 'Mara' Coldharbour has spent fifteen years outrunning her family's name, ferrying medicine and gossip along a river that keeps its secrets. When floodwaters surrender a salvage chest bearing the seal of Vessany — a drowned nation her grandfather helped sink — Mara becomes the unwilling heir to coordinates everyone wants and no one survives claiming. Hunted by the salvage fleet's ruthless broker across six tides, she must decide whether inheritance is a birthright or a debt. In the end, Mara reaches the wreck first but burns the manifest, choosing to let the dead nation stay dead — and finally claims a life measured in years, not miles.
about_author: Mara Oyelaran is a former river-guide turned writer who grew up in trading towns where maps were treated as rumors. She writes adventure fiction about people who inherit more than they asked for.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A routine med-run ends when floodwater spits a sealed chest onto her landing strip, stamped with Vessany's long-dead national seal. Inside: half a chart and a tide-table marked six days out. The emotional beat is wary curiosity hardening into dread as she recognizes her grandfather's handwriting on the margin.

chapters.title: The Broker's Wake
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A black-hulled salvage ship enters the delta asking questions about wreckage. Mara lies badly to its broker, Adeyemi Voss, who offers to buy the chest sight unseen — proof he already knows it exists. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance as she realizes silence is no longer an option.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Sank
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with a letter from 1961 interleaved. At her estranged aunt's houseboat, Mara learns the Coldharbour family guided the scuttling of the Vessany treasury to end a war — and kept the chart as blackmail. Beat: grief and shame colliding; inheritance revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: Medicine for Lies
chapters.summary: Tunde's POV, a river doctor and Mara's oldest friend. He patches a wounded deckhand who escaped Voss's ship and confirms the fleet is bribing every settlement for word of a woman pilot. Tunde urges Mara to hand it over. Beat: loyalty tested; Mara chooses flight, straining their friendship.

chapters.title: The Narrows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A cat-and-mouse flight through fog-choked gorges as Voss's seaplane shadows her. She trades altitude for distance and cracks a strut, crash-landing at an abandoned mission. Beat: exhilaration curdling into cost — survival now demands sacrifice of the plane, her freedom's symbol.

chapters.title: The Mission at Kilometre Zero
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Repairing the strut with mission scraps, she meets Brother Elias, last keeper of the Vessany refugees' memory, who reveals the chest holds not gold but names — the drowned nation's true ledger of the betrayed. Beat: purpose shifting from escape to witness.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Adeyemi Voss's POV. We learn his own grandfather drowned with Vessany, and he wants the ledger to restore his family's honor by any means. He captures Tunde as leverage. Beat: the antagonist humanized even as his methods corrupt him — power justifying itself.

chapters.title: Trade of Blood
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The exchange at a mid-river shoal goes wrong; Tunde takes a bullet shielding Mara, and she escapes only by burning Voss's fuel barge. Beat: rage and guilt — the price of survival paid in other people's blood.

chapters.title: The Wreck of Vessany
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, final tide. Diving the flooded cathedral-hold at slack water, she finds the vault empty except for the second half of the chart — which points back upriver, to her own family's boathouse. Voss arrives armed. Beat: climax; revelation that the treasure was always home.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the boathouse vault they find the ledger; Mara reads the names aloud and lets Voss copy them freely, refusing to trade memory for power. Voss, offered exactly what he claimed to want, cannot accept grace and leaves empty-handed. Tunde recovers; Mara stays put for the first time in fifteen years. Beat: resolution — inheritance transformed from debt into duty, and a life finally rooted.
